news.Title: ONTO Beats Q3 Estimates & Uplifts View: Buy, Hold or Sell the Stock?
news.Content:
Onto Innovation Inc. ONTO delivered stronger-than-expected third-quarter 2026 results, with revenues, operating margin and earnings per share exceeding the high end of management's guidance. Strong demand for AI-related semiconductor manufacturing equipment, growing adoption of its Dragonfly inspection platform and rising investments in advanced packaging supported the performance. Revenues reached $410 million, up nearly 90% year over year and 19% sequentially.

Non-GAAP earnings per share increased to $2.44 from 92 cents in the prior-year quarter, while non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 32.6% from 21.1%. Non-GAAP gross margin reached 57.6%, increasing 60 bps sequentially and 360 bps year over year. Continued margin expansion could support further earnings growth if demand remains strong and ONTO maintains operating efficiency. The company's outlook also strengthened, with management raising its fourth-quarter revenue expectations and reporting a record backlog of more than $1.3 billion. Improving customer visibility, expanding product adoption and operational efficiencies are expected to support growth through 2027.

In response to a record third quarter, ONTO's shares jumped 12% in last day's trading and closed at $194.04. Shares also went up 6% in pre-market trading today. ONTO's shares have risen 45.4% in the past year compared with the Zacks Nanotechnology industry's growth of 46.5%. The company has outpaced the Zacks Computer and Technology sector and the S&P 500 composite's growth of 6.4% and 0.9%, respectively.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

ONTO's key competitors include KLA Corporation KLAC, Camtek Ltd CAMT and Applied Materials AMAT. KLAC, CAMT, and AMAT grew 27.1%, 0.9%, and 62%, respectively, over the same period.

However, after this strong performance, investors may question whether ONTO shares still have room to rise. Let's examine the company's growth drivers, financial performance and potential risks to assess its investment prospects.

Strong Q3 Results Highlight ONTO's Growth Momentum

The results reflect strong demand across the company's product portfolio. Advanced packaging and specialty device products were the key contributors, with revenues increasing 35% sequentially. These businesses accounted for slightly more than half of total quarterly revenues, led by continued Dragonfly adoption and a recovery in power and specialty device inspection demand. Advanced-node revenues reached approximately $135 million, with memory contributing about 60% and logic accounting for the remaining 40%. Software and services generated roughly $60 million.

Story Continues

An encouraging indicator is Onto Innovation's backlog, which increased to more than $1.3 billion during the third quarter. Management cited strong customer demand and visibility into investment plans extending multiple years. It expects full-year 2026 revenue growth to exceed 45% year over year and anticipates sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027. These expectations are backed by demand for advanced packaging, increasingly sophisticated logic and memory devices, and inspection technologies that help manufacturers improve process control. Management also expects advanced packaging revenues to grow more than 80% in 2026, while Advanced Nodes revenues are expected to increase more than 35%. These projections highlight the breadth of the company's growth opportunities.

The Dragonfly platform, especially G5, led growth, supporting high-resolution applications with more than 10 customers and orders extending into 2027. The G5 platform is increasingly adopted for new applications, with revenues doubling compared with 2025, while G3 remains relevant for lower-end needs. ONTO also reported strong momentum in power semiconductors and silicon photonics. Combined revenues from these markets doubled in the third quarter, with management expecting significant growth in the fourth quarter and into the first half of 2027.

Onto Innovation Inc. Price and Consensus

Onto Innovation Inc. price-consensus-chart | Onto Innovation Inc. Quote

The strong order visibility prompted ONTO to raise its fourth-quarter 2026 revenue outlook. It expects fourth-quarter revenues of $430-$450 million, representing more than 7% sequential growth at the midpoint. At the midpoint of its guidance, gross margin is expected to improve around 50 bps sequentially to slightly above 58%, while operating margin is projected to reach 34%. ONTO also forecasts non-GAAP EPS of $2.69.

For full-year 2026, management expects revenues of about $1.485 billion at the midpoint, representing growth of more than 45%. Looking ahead, ONTO anticipates sequential revenue growth through at least the first half of 2027, supported by strong customer commitments, broader product adoption and a growing backlog.

What Could Limit ONTO's Growth Upside?

Despite its strong growth outlook, it faces several risks that investors should consider. Onto Innovation faces several cost and operational headwinds, including rising memory and component prices, higher freight expenses, tariffs and dependence on certain single-source components. Although the company is addressing these challenges through product design changes, localized supply chains, supplier partnerships and operational efficiencies, persistent cost pressures or component shortages could affect margins and equipment deliveries.

Demand uncertainty is another risk, as any slowdown or delay in data center and AI infrastructure investments could weaken customer spending and order momentum. In addition, technology transitions, including upgrades to newer inspection systems and evolving advanced packaging methods, require continuous innovation and operational adjustments. While productivity improvements, extended factory models and supply-chain initiatives have helped mitigate these pressures, their impact on profitability and growth remains worth monitoring.

Additionally, the company must manage execution and delivery risks to convert its record backlog into revenues on schedule. Rapid technological changes and competition in inspection and metrology also require continued innovation to maintain its position in advanced packaging and advanced-node markets.

Valuation risk

Strong growth expectations may already be reflected in the stock price. Even solid earnings results may not produce additional upside if expectations are too high. In terms of forward price/earnings, ONTO's shares are trading at 17.32X, higher than the industry's 3.37X.

KLAC, CAMT and AMAT are trading at multiples of 24.44X, 23.72X and 20.12X, respectively.

Estimate Revision Trend for ONTO

Earnings estimates for ONTO have been stagnant for both 2026 and 2027 over the past 60 days.

ONTO Stock After Q3 Results: Buy, Hold or Sell?

ONTO's record backlog, AI-driven demand and higher 2027 growth visibility support a bullish business outlook, but the stock's valuation and execution risks matter before making a Buy call. Investors should monitor the sustainability of AI-related semiconductor spending, customer investment plans, execution as the company scales and its ability to maintain margin expansion. The company's strong operating outlook is encouraging, but the potential for further stock gains also depends on its valuation and market expectations.

Existing shareholders may consider holding the stock as long as the company's growth outlook remains strong and its valuation is reasonable. With a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), ONTO appears to be treading in the middle of the road, and new investors may be better off trading with caution. news.Title: ASTS Q3 Earnings Miss Estimates as Higher Costs Offset Revenue Growth
news.Content:
AST SpaceMobile, Inc. ASTS reported lackluster third-quarter 2026 results, with both earnings and revenues missing the Zacks Consensus Estimate. The company reported a loss of 44 cents per share, wider than the consensus estimate of a loss of 41 cents, representing a negative surprise of 7.3%. However, the loss narrowed from 45 cents per share in the year-ago quarter.

Quarterly revenues surged 187.1% year over year to $42.32 million but missed the consensus estimate of $44.47 million by 4.8%. Growth was driven by commercial gateway deliveries and U.S. government contract milestones. However, elevated operating expenses continued to pressure profitability.

ASTS Sees Robust Growth Across Revenue Streams

Product revenues increased 165.6% year over year to $20.57 million from $7.75 million in the prior-year quarter. Growth was primarily driven by commercial gateway equipment deliveries to mobile network operator partners as the company expanded its ground infrastructure.

Service revenues surged 211% to $21.75 million from $6.99 million a year ago. The increase reflected progress in U.S. government programs and the achievement of contractual milestones. The company continues to benefit from growing demand for its space-based communication and sensing capabilities.

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

AST SpaceMobile, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | AST SpaceMobile, Inc. Quote

AST SpaceMobile's Operating Costs Remain Elevated

Total operating expenses increased 123.5% year over year to $211.03 million from $94.42 million. Engineering services costs surged 134.6% to $95.79 million, reflecting investments in satellite manufacturing, workforce expansion and network development.

General and administrative expenses increased 86.8% to $55.71 million. Research and development expenses rose to $9.09 million from $5.53 million. Depreciation and amortization expenses increased to $25.08 million from $12.72 million.

Adjusted operating expenses were $133.6 million, up from $119.1 million in the preceding quarter. Excluding adjusted cost of revenues, adjusted operating expenses totaled $109.4 million, within management's previously guided range of $105 million to $115 million.

ASTS Advances Satellite Manufacturing and Deployment

AST SpaceMobile accelerated its satellite manufacturing roadmap by advancing next-generation application-specific integrated circuit (ASIC) integration to BlueBird 34 from the originally planned BlueBird 50. The upgraded technology is expected to deliver a 10-fold improvement in processing bandwidth compared with its existing Block 1 satellites.

The company is manufacturing satellites through BlueBird 51 at its Texas facilities. Two factories are operating full shifts, supporting management's target of producing six ASIC-enabled satellites monthly by December 2026.

Story Continues

BlueBirds 14, 15 and 16 have been shipped to Cape Canaveral, while additional satellite shipments are planned through January 2027. Management targets approximately 45 BlueBird satellites in orbit by mid-2027, with launch agreements covering more than 100 satellites for deployment during 2027 and 2028.

AST SpaceMobile Expands Commercial and Government Reach

The company expects to activate intermittent nationwide satellite broadband coverage in the United States and other key markets before the end of 2026. Initial rollout markets include Canada, Japan, Saudi Arabia and the United Kingdom.

AST SpaceMobile has agreements with more than 60 mobile network operators representing over three billion subscribers globally. It also successfully validated satellite beam handovers between terrestrial and space-based cellular networks with AT&T, marking an important step toward commercial service deployment.

Government opportunities are expanding. The company secured an approximately $100 million U.S. Space Force contract for advanced space-based sensing capabilities. It also announced approximately $1 billion in non-dilutive Japanese government funding to support mid-band satellite manufacturing and launches.

ASTS Maintains Strong Liquidity Amid Heavy Investments

As of Sept. 30, 2026, AST SpaceMobile held approximately $3.23 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash. Long-term debt, excluding the current portion, stood at $4.08 billion compared with $2.21 billion at the end of 2025.

Capital expenditures totaled approximately $310 million during the third quarter, down from approximately $610 million in the preceding quarter. The lower spending primarily reflected timing-related shifts in launch payments.

The company also announced Blacklift, its planned reusable rocket capable of carrying up to five BlueBird satellites per launch. Initial launches are targeted for late 2028, potentially providing greater control over satellite deployment schedules.

AST SpaceMobile Reaffirms 2026 Revenue Outlook

Management reiterated its full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $150 million to $200 million, with potential upside from recently signed contracts. Revenue generation is expected to benefit from gateway deliveries, government contract milestones, consulting services and software licensing.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, AST SpaceMobile expects adjusted operating expenses, excluding adjusted cost of revenues, between $130 million and $140 million. news.Title: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold HPE Stock at a P/E Multiple of 10.08X?
news.Content:
Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE trades at a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 10.08X, below the Zacks Computer and Technology sector's P/E of 16.76X. The discounted valuation of HPE stock is further substantiated by the Zacks Value Score of A.

HPE Forward 12-Month (P/S) Valuation Chart

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The discounted valuation remains despite HPE stock climbing 98% year to date, outperforming the broader sector and the Zacks Computer - Integrated Systems industry's return of 65.2% and 4.1%, respectively.

HPE YTD Performance Chart

HPE Experiences Growth Across Cloud and Networking

Hewlett Packard Enterprise operates across three primary business segments, namely Cloud & AI, Networking, and Corporate Investments and Other, serving enterprise customers with infrastructure, software, services and flexible consumption solutions. Cloud & AI combines HPE's server, storage and financial services businesses.

HPE's server portfolio includes general-purpose and workload-optimized systems, high-performance computing, supercomputing, AI infrastructure, data analytics and transaction processing. Its storage offerings include HPE Alletra, unstructured data solutions, data protection, GreenLake Flex and related software. The segment is benefiting from growing demand for AI-ready servers and enterprise infrastructure. In the third quarter of fiscal 2026, Cloud & AI generated $9.04 billion in revenues, up 25.4% year over year.

HPE's networking develops and sells network and security products and services across campus, branch, data center, routing and security markets. Its portfolio includes wireless access points, switches, routers, gateways, network-management software, support and professional services. The acquisition of Juniper Networks has expanded HPE's networking capabilities and exposure to AI data center infrastructure. HPE's networking revenues reached $2.89 billion in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, rising 10% on a normalized basis.

Corporate Investments and Other includes Advisory and Professional Services, Telco, Instant On and Hewlett Packard Labs. These activities complement HPE's broader technology portfolio through consulting, specialized connectivity offerings and research. Across these businesses, HPE is also expanding GreenLake, its consumption-based hybrid cloud platform, connecting infrastructure, software and services. Together, its three segments position HPE to address demand for AI infrastructure, modern networking and hybrid cloud environments.

Story Continues

HPE Wins Against Competitors With Diverse Portfolio

HPE competes with Super Micro Computer SMCI, Dell Technologies DELL and Cisco CSCO in the AI infrastructure market. However, HPE's ability to package compute, storage, networking and services into pre-configured solutions can reduce deployment complexity for enterprises and sovereign customers while giving it an edge over its competitors. Super Micro Computer is on track to scale rack production capacity to more than 6,000 AI racks per month by the end of fiscal 2026, including 3,000 direct liquid cooling racks monthly.

Super Micro Computer is already shipping 150kW AI racks in volume and preparing 250kW and 500kW rack solutions to support future high-density AI training and inference workloads. Dell Technologies is a major supplier of servers and storage systems, with a broad customer base across enterprises and cloud providers. Its scale, established distribution and service offerings give it an edge in winning large contracts.

Cisco has also taken $5.3 billion of hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders in fiscal 2026 and raised its full-year order outlook to $9 billion from $5 billion. However, HPE's ability to package compute, storage, networking and services into pre-configured solutions can reduce deployment complexity for enterprises and sovereign customers. This gives HPE an edge over its competitors.

HPE is also able to keep its margin stable. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for HPE's fiscal 2026 margin reflects year-over-year growth of 97%. Estimates have been revised upward over the past 30 days.

Conclusion: Buy HPE Stock Now

Hewlett Packard Enterprise's strong AI infrastructure momentum, expanding AI backlog, growing GreenLake adoption and integrated portfolio support its growth outlook. Despite a sharp share price rally, HPE's valuation remains attractive relative to industry peers. Given these factors, it's prudent to accumulate this Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) stock at present. news.Content: 隨美股科技股拉回與台股震盪加劇，日股抗震指標復華日本龍頭（00949）首度配息開出紅盤，擬每單位配發 3.02 元，實拿年配息率高達 13.65%！00949 精選具備國際護城河優勢的日本巨頭，近月展現極佳抗跌韌性。本文完整解析 00949 首配亮點、特色、成分股，作為日股投資人的參考！ *本文統整公開資訊僅供參考，本文提及之歷史數據統計，不代表未來投資之績效，投資人應審慎考量本身之需求與投資風險。 *高股息ETF「無保證收益及配息」，提醒投資人高股息ETF並非「定存替代」。 一、巴菲特買日本股票 根據 CNBC 的資料，巴菲特（Warren Buffett）及其公司波克夏·海瑟威在日本股市投資了日本五大綜合商社： 伊藤忠商事、丸紅、三菱商事、三井物產和住友商事 ，且明確表示將長期持有這些股票，也進一步將投資額度擴大至最初 10% 的上限。 日本股票護城河 日本龍頭股票普遍具有以下特色，形成了企業護城河： 完整介紹請見： 豐雲學堂ETF怎麼買專欄 這些因素鞏固長期競爭優勢與投資價值，這也是巴菲特青睞日本股市的原因之一。 舉個例子：日本許多企業在全球市場具備領先的產業地位，像是豐田汽車是全球最大汽車製造商之一、而且海外版圖也大，公司海外營收佔比達70%。

news.Title: AI晶片股回神！韓日領軍反彈、台股祭限空令終結連七跌 市場緊盯CPI
news.Content:
亞洲股市周二(10日)延續全球科技股強勁反彈走勢，南韓與日本股市領漲，台股終結連七日跌勢。但由於輝達(NVDA-US)執行長黃仁勳相關風波未明朗，加上美國通膨報告即將公布，投資人對這波反彈能否續航仍抱持審慎態度。

在華爾街創下約七個月來最大單日漲幅後，投資人正在重新買進先前遭重挫的晶片股。美國總統川普則釋出訊號，若與伊朗談判取得進展，美國不太可能再度發動攻擊，帶動油價進一步回落，緩解通膨疑慮也提振市場情緒。

MSCI亞太指數盤中上漲2%，南韓KOSPI指數大漲逾4%，日本日經225指數上漲超過2%，東證股價指數(TOPIX)上漲2.2%。

亞洲交易時段，那斯達克100期貨微跌不到0.1%，標普500期貨小漲0.15%。

韓股部分，SK海力士股價上漲6.3%，三星電子上漲4.9%。日股方面，鎧俠(Kioxia)上漲6.6%，TDK上漲5.2%，村田製作所上漲5.9%，LG Innotek上漲5.1%。

台灣加權指數盤中漲幅一度達6.4%，終場漲幅仍有2.5%。台積電(2330-TW)上漲2.2%，大立光(3008-TW)上漲2.8%，鴻海(2317-TW)上漲2.5%。

台股到周一為止已連七日下跌，創2022年以來最長連跌紀錄，周二終於止跌反彈。台灣金管會將放空額度上限從原本前30日平均成交量的30%調降至3%，並將最低融資保證金成數從90%提高至130%，同時維持最高新台幣5000億元(約152億美元)穩定市場基金可供運用。

日本與台灣股市上周均進入熊市，南韓股市則較夏季高點下跌逾40%，三星電子與SK海力士股價一度累計下跌逾16%。

美國10月消費者物價指數(CPI)將於周二公布，市場預期整體CPI與核心CPI將分別月增0.3%及0.2%。目前市場對聯準會(Fed)升息的預期機率已從一周前的74%升至84%。

另外，Anthropic周二可能展開的首次公開發行(IPO)投資人說明會，上市計畫，尋求最高693億美元估值，Anthropic上市計畫與本周稍晚的與CoreWeave(CRWV-US)財報，將成為觀察AI投資人意願的重要指標。

news.Title: 不演了？ 台股漲幅大收斂 他追旺宏、華邦電秒被套
news.Content:
台股今（10）日早盤跳空開高，盤中一度大漲逾1400點，不過隨著時間推移，漲勢一度逐漸收斂近千點，所幸在台積電由黑翻紅，也日月光、南亞、台達電重新鎖回漲停下，成功守住42000點大關。

台股上周歷經重挫回檔，指數一度摜破38000點，周一則迎來報復性反彈，今日則延續漲勢，早盤一度大漲逾1400點，雖然衝上43135點高點後一路下滑，漲勢收斂逾千點，但在觸及41930點後，在權值股集體拉抬下，指數又再度上揚400點，於42300點附近震盪；截至上午11:55點暫報42312點，上漲654點，漲幅1.57%。

權值股部分，台積電開高震盪，早盤衝上2280元後震盪走低，盤中甚至一度翻黑，但隨即又迅速翻紅成功，小漲5元，暫報2240元；台達電、南亞、日月光等權值股在大筆賣單下也一度漲停打開，不過後續又成功亮燈漲停。

針對今日的盤勢，有股民在臉書社團「當沖勒戒所」發文分享，早上看大漲於是衝進去買旺宏、華邦電，沒想到漲勢收斂，現賣現套「今天早上進場買旺宏、華邦電，馬上賠錢。」

留言區網友紛紛安慰，「平常心吧！很多人成交後，眼睜睜看著股價開始往下掉，笑你的人也發生過啦！」、「沒事的 當沖華邦電現在懊悔中」、「我買0050都能大賠了」；也有網友表示，「追高殺低才是真散戶」、「韭韭的」、「韭菜來了」。

（封面圖／東森新聞）

news.Title: 《日股早盤》AI/半導體飆 日經衝1,700點；MLCC嗨

MoneyDJ新聞 2026-11-10 10:37:50 蔡承啟 發佈

跟隨美股昨日(9日)走揚腳步，日本AI、半導體相關股飆漲，激勵日經225指數10日大漲，收復6萬點整數大關，早盤收盤(台北時間上午10點30分)大漲2.89%或漲1,700.28點，暫收60,475.78點。

東證股價指數(TOPIX)早盤收盤大漲2.22%或漲84.69點，暫收3,902.85點。

截至早盤收盤為止，東證Prime上漲家數1,208家、下跌家數320家、維持平盤家數17家。東證Prime成交額為4兆2,293億日圓。

就類股表現來看，截至早盤收盤為止，全部33類股中、有26類股上漲，其中以非鐵金屬類股漲幅最大，其次依序為銀行業、電機業和玻璃土石製品。

根據MoneyDJ XQ全球贏家系統的報價顯示，截至日本股市10日早盤收盤(台北時間上午10點30分)為止，日圓相對於美元匯率貶值0.14%至158.05日圓兌1美元；日圓相對於美元匯率9日升值0.40%，4個交易日來第3度走升。

就個股表現來看，NAND Flash廠鎧俠(Kioxia)早盤飆漲6.62%、晶片設備巨擘東京威力科創(TEL)早盤飆漲5.71%、測試設備商愛德萬測試(Advantest)早盤大漲3.91%、晶圓切割機廠DISCO早盤飆漲6.76%、生產AI資料中心用光纖的Fujikura早盤飆漲6.07%。

古河電工(Furukawa Electric)早盤狂飆7.90%。 AI需求旺、供不應求，古河電工擴充台灣、日本銅箔產能，目標將供應能力倍增，且古河電工上修今年度財測預估。

夏普(Sharp)早盤跌1.49%。 零組件價格飆漲，夏普上季純益暴減近6成，而夏普維持今年度財測預估不變，且表示AI伺服器最快將在2026年度末開始交貨。

半導體材料商JX金屬(JX Advanced Metals)早盤上漲1.88%。 AI需求加持，JX金屬上修今年度財測預估，且稱「AI需求未放緩」。

news.Title: 台積電營收出爐前...股價漲45元「市值重返59兆元大關」 1天增加一家南亞科
news.Content:
台積電（2330）10月營收於今（10）日下午出爐！在市場買盤與卡位資金強勢湧入下，台積電今日盤中強勢衝上 2,280元，上漲45元，漲幅超過2%，伴隨股價走揚，台積電整體市值也從 57.95 兆元直接衝上 59.11 兆元大關，光是單日市值就狂增逾1兆元，相當於一天拉出一整家南亞科的總市值，使市值重新站穩59兆元整數關卡。

資深台股分析師蔡明翰表示，輝達執行長黃仁勳陷入桃色風波，昨日輝達（Nvidia）釋出負面訊息引發修正，台積電今早表現卻展現極強韌性，雖然輝達與台積電連動度極高，致使昨日台積電 ADR 表現相對費城半導體指數略顯疲弱，但關鍵在於「該利空並未在整體半導體族群中擴散」，且費半指數終場仍強勢大漲。

蔡明翰指出，輝達昨日開低後並未一路下殺，反而出現強烈的開低拉回支撐，顯示市場對於10月至11月這波AI 族群大幅修正的「利空已出現鈍化現象」。當市場對利空不再過度恐慌，代表股市底部位階已經逐步確認，資金自然會重新回流核心績優股。因此只要輝達沒有發生實質性產業風暴，情緒未進一步惡化，這波大幅修正期已告一段落，對台股與台積電後市絕對是正面利多。

針對投資人的後續操作策略，蔡明翰提出兩大核心觀察點，第一，利空不跌即是底：市場目前已不再將輝達個案消息視為無差別利空解讀，AI 供應鏈最壞情況漸過，投資人毋須過度恐慌；第二，留意本周美股 CoreWeave 財報：身為 AI 算力基礎設施指標的 CoreWeave 即將公布財報，市場普遍預期其本業仍處虧損且資本支出龐大，若財報公布後市場能以「利空出盡」或理性態度消化，將進一步奠定AI族群築底反彈的堅實基礎。

陳依旻／財經特派記者副組長，主跑央行、證交所、投信投顧等

news.Title: KOSPI早盤大漲5.1%，韓交所啟動買方Sidecar
news.Content:
【財訊快報／陳孟朔】韓國股市週二(10日)早盤強勁反彈，韓國綜合股價指數(KOSPI)漲幅擴大至5.1%，報5,276.81點，站上5,200點。韓國交易所隨即啟動買方Sidecar，暫停程式交易買單。買方Sidecar是韓股期貨急漲時啟動的交易措施，暫停範圍限於程式交易買單，其他交易仍可進行。

隔夜美股科技股走強，那指收漲2.74%，費城半導體指數大漲6.85%，為亞洲科技股早盤反彈提供助力。費半上週重挫逾12%，週一由超微與博通帶動回升。

韓股上週曾因AI投資前景疑慮遭遇賣壓，半導體權值股首當其衝。週二大盤急彈後，三星電子與SK海力士能否延續反彈，仍是觀察韓股漲勢的重點。

news.Title: Lantronix, Inc. (LTRX) Tops Q1 Earnings and Revenue Estimates
news.Content:
Lantronix, Inc. (LTRX) came out with quarterly earnings of $0.05 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $0.04 per share. This compares to earnings of $0.04 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +25.00%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this company would post earnings of $0.04 per share when it actually produced earnings of $0.04, delivering no surprise.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates two times.

Lantronix, which belongs to the Zacks Computer - Networking industry, posted revenues of $32.37 million for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 0.53%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $29.79 million. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates two times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Lantronix shares have lost about 11.9% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 7.8%.

What's Next for Lantronix?

While Lantronix has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Lantronix was mixed. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to perform in line with the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $0.04 on $34 million in revenues for the coming quarter and $0.22 on $135.4 million in revenues for the current fiscal year.

Story Continues

Investors should be mindful of the fact that the outlook for the industry can have a material impact on the performance of the stock as well. In terms of the Zacks Industry Rank, Computer - Networking is currently in the top 18% of the 250 plus Zacks industries. Our research shows that the top 50% of the Zacks-ranked industries outperform the bottom 50% by a factor of more than 2 to 1.

Cisco Systems (CSCO), another stock in the same industry, has yet to report results for the quarter ended October 2026. The results are expected to be released on November 12.

This seller of routers, switches, software and services is expected to post quarterly earnings of $1.33 per share in its upcoming report, which represents a year-over-year change of +33%. The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days.

Cisco Systems' revenues are expected to be $18.09 billion, up 21.5% from the year-ago quarter.

news.Title: Will Cisco Systems (CSCO) Deliver the Strong Results the Market Needs to See?
news.Content:
With technology stocks recently coming under pressure amid concerns about lofty AI valuations, potential regulatory scrutiny, and immense infrastructure spending, Cisco Systems CSCO) will be among the most important AI-related companies reporting earnings this week.

While CSCO has not escaped the recent selloff, its strong year-to-date performance underscores investors' renewed enthusiasm for established networking and hardware companies.

Cisco's success highlights how the AI infrastructure buildout has revitalized longstanding technology leaders, including Dell Technologies DELL) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise HPE), whose networking, servers, and computing hardware have become increasingly critical to AI data centers.

With Cisco scheduled to report its fiscal first-quarter results after market hours on Thursday, November 12, expectations are high for another strong quarter.

Cisco's Q1 Expectations

Cisco is expected to report Q1 adjusted earnings of $1.33 per share, representing 33% year-over-year growth from EPS of $1.00 in the prior-year quarter. This comes as Q1 revenue is projected to increase nearly 22% to $18.09 billion from $14.88 billion a year ago.

Momentum has been impressive, with Cisco's fiscal Q4 revenue rising 18% to $17.25 billion and adjusted EPS jumping 23% to $1.22.

More importantly, Cisco is benefiting from accelerating demand for AI networking infrastructure. The company secured $9.3 billion in AI infrastructure orders during fiscal 2026 and expects AI-related revenue from hyperscalers to reach $7.5 billion in its current FY27, up from approximately $4 billion last year.

Investors will be closely watching whether this momentum can support another guidance increase, particularly as growing sales of lower-margin AI networking hardware could pressure overall gross margins.

CSCO Performance & Valuation Comparison

Despite the recent tech selloff, Cisco stock has still gained nearly 30% YTD, comfortably outperforming the benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq's returns of just under 10%.

Over the last three years, CSCO has delivered a total return of more than 100% when including dividends, compared with roughly 80% for the broader indexes.

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

At current levels of just under $100 a share, CSCO trades at 20X forward earnings, which is roughly on par with its Zacks Computer-Networking Industry average and near the S&P 500's 18X.

This suggests investors aren't paying an excessive premium for Cisco's expanding AI exposure, although its valuation is no longer as inexpensive as it was before the AI infrastructure spending boom. While CSCO trades above its decade-long median of 16X forward earnings, shares are still more than 35% below a high of 32X during this period.

Story Continues

Cisco's Generous Dividend

Intriguingly, Cisco offers a compelling income opportunity that remains relatively uncommon among major AI infrastructure beneficiaries and many tech stocks in general.

Its quarterly dividend of $0.42 per share equates to an annual payout of $1.68 and a yield approaching 2%, providing additional appeal for long-term investors.

Bottom Line: Can Cisco Keep Its Momentum?

Sporting a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) , Cisco Systems remains an attractive way to capitalize on the AI infrastructure buildout without paying the premium valuations often associated with semiconductor and software stocks.

Strong quarterly results and upbeat guidance could reinforce confidence in Cisco's AI-driven growth trajectory while providing much-needed reassurance to investors following the broader tech selloff. However, sustained revenue growth and healthy margins will be essential to maintaining the stock's resilient momentum.

news.Title: Brave’s Leo assistant uses NEAR AI to prove its AI chats stay private, paving the way for businesses to use AI with sensitive data
news.Content:
Most of the AI tools businesses have adopted so far handle low-risk work, such as drafting emails, summarizing calls and cleaning up slide decks.

The material companies would most like to hand over is the material they guard most closely.

That includes financial research before it's published, legal files covered by attorney-client privilege and internal data on pricing, products and deals.

What holds that work back is usually not what the models can do. It's what happens to the data once it leaves the building.

Sending a confidential document to an AI model means trusting the cloud provider, the chip operator and the AI company not to see it. Most of the time, that trust rests on a privacy policy.

Related: Bernie Sanders spots opportunity as 66% of Americans oppose AI data centers

The pressure is showing up in corporate budgets. In Cisco's 2026 Data and Privacy Benchmark Study , 90% of the more than 5,200 IT and security professionals surveyed said their privacy programs have expanded because of AI. Cisco puts it plainly:

"AI ambition is outpacing readiness."

The cost of getting it wrong is rising too. IBM's 2026 Cost of a Data Breach Report puts the average breach at $4.99 million, a record. Attacks that pull sensitive data back out of AI models cost even more, at $6 million on average.

NEAR AI , the AI arm of the NEAR ecosystem, is building its business around replacing that policy with proof.

On October 15, the company announced that Leo, the AI assistant built into the Brave browser, now runs on private inference from NEAR AI Cloud.

Inference is the step where a model reads a prompt and produces an answer, and it's where user data is most exposed.

A locked room the operator can't enter

According to NEAR AI, Leo conversations on the GLM 5.3 Flash model run inside trusted execution environments, or TEEs.

A TEE is a walled-off section of a processor where code and data are shielded from the rest of the machine. NEAR AI says its TEEs are built on Intel TDX and NVIDIA Confidential Compute.

The company says the cloud host, the GPU operator and NEAR AI itself are "cryptographically locked out." Leo encrypts each prompt in the browser with a protocol called Oblivious HTTP, using a key that exists only inside the enclave.

Brave's relay strips the user's IP address before passing the request on. NEAR AI says memory stays encrypted while the model runs, and every response is signed inside the enclave.

The bigger point is who does the checking. Before Leo receives the enclave's key, Brave's own open-source verifier checks the hardware against Intel's signature and NVIDIA 's attestation service.

Story Continues

Attestation is a cryptographic proof of what hardware and software are running.

The verifier also rebuilds NEAR AI's code from public source to confirm it matches what is deployed. As the post puts it: "No pass, no key."

NEAR AI's Trust Center puts it in business terms. It says privacy is "enforced by hardware, not policy," and verifiable through attestation "checked against Intel and NVIDIA, not NEAR AI."

Trending on TheStreet Roundtable:

Veteran economist says investors are watching the wrong bubble

Billionaire Ray Dalio sounds alarm on AI's $4.4 trillion debt squeeze

Two big U.S.-listed Bitcoin miners plan major exit for AI

Brave's reach as a distribution channel

Distribution may matter as much as the technology. Privacy tools usually struggle because users have to go find them. Inside a browser, private inference becomes a setting.

Brave currently serves over 130 million monthly active users . That figure shows the size of the potential audience.

Private inference applies only to Brave Leo users who choose GLM 5.3 Flash in the model settings.

The rollout came in stages. Brave began testing NEAR AI's TEEs in November 2025 with DeepSeek V3.1 in Brave Nightly, its experimental build. The October release takes it to the full production browser.

Brendan Eich, co-founder and CEO of Brave, called the integration "a first for AI chats in browsers." Illia Polosukhin, co-founder of NEAR, framed it as a question of ownership.

"Browsers are a primary computing interface that handles all of our personal information, so it's critical that AI is introduced in a user-owned way," Polosukhin said.

NEAR AI says Brave joins Venice AI, Abound and the Government of Bermuda among organizations running production workloads on NEAR AI Cloud.

That mix of consumer apps and a public-sector user hints at the same distribution model at work: privacy delivered through software people already use, rather than a standalone product.

Guarantees that stop at the model

For businesses weighing sensitive workloads, the fine print matters. The privacy guarantee in the

Brave announcement covers one model in one deployment. NEAR AI describes GLM 5.3 Flash as an open-weights model under the MIT license, meaning its underlying parameters are public.

NEAR AI's Trust Center specifies that open-weight models hosted by NEAR AI run inside the TEEs. Third-party models are also offered, but NEAR AI says those are "proxied without revealing the customer's identity and processed under the provider's own data terms."

In other words, the hardware guarantee applies only where NEAR AI controls the hardware.

That distinction will likely shape how companies buy. A guarantee tied to a named model, a named deployment and an attestation anyone can check gives them something to audit.

NEAR AI also says a hardware-attested deployment log confirms that the model a user picks is the one answering.

Publishing open-source verification and relying on chipmakers' attestation services rather than its own word lets NEAR AI's approach be tested from outside.

For businesses that have kept their most sensitive files away from AI, that offers a way to bring them in without taking anyone's word for it.

Related: $13 trillion brokerage giant offers cheapest ways to trade crypto

Intel took 25 years to get back to its dot-com peak — and lost it in 6 months: Chart of the Day
news.Content:
Half off sounds like a deal. On Wall Street, it can be the start of a much bigger sale.

Right now, Intel ( INTC ), Arm ( ARM ), Sandisk ( SNDK ), and CoreWeave ( CRWV ) are among the AI darlings trading at less than half their 2026 highs, and chip stocks just lost nearly 30% in five weeks .

Chip stocks bounced Friday and roared back Monday. The PHLX Semiconductor Index ( ^SOX ) jumped about 7%, its best day since July, and the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) rose more than 2%, its biggest gain since April.

Veteran trader Michael Martin isn't biting. "Lower prices mean lower market cap. It doesn't mean better value," said Martin, founder of TraderMindset.com, who works with Wall Street legend Victor "Trader Vic" Sperandeo .

"I keep hearing Gordon Gekko's voice in the back of my mind — 'A fool and their money are lucky to get together in the first place,' " he told Yahoo Finance.

His bigger worry is traders who talk themselves into holding on. "Don't confuse investor language with trader language," he said. "If you're a trader, be a trader."

Intel's long, strange trip

Martin's favorite example is Intel. "A lot of people think like, wow, Intel was 125. I can get it now for half that. It's a bargain," he said. "But at 55 or whatever it is, you can see 40 long before you're gonna see 140."

Intel's own history backs him up. The stock peaked at about $75 in August 2000, was down to half by October, and kept going, bottoming near $13 in 2002.

It didn't close above that dot-com peak again until April 24, 2026 . Loyal holders got a victory lap to about $141 in June before the AI selloff dragged the stock back below its old high on Oct. 30. Intel closed Monday at about $59, still up roughly 60% this year.

Intel had plenty of company. Five other dot-com leaders also kept falling after first being cut in half, from another 30% for Microsoft ( MSFT ) to another 88% for Amazon ( AMZN ), according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

None of that makes investor language wrong. Amazon now trades at nearly 50 times its 2000 peak.

But that's an investor's clock. Trouble starts when a trade gets judged on one.

How to keep a trade from becoming an accident

Martin, a discretionary trader for four decades, offers guidelines, not rules.

Size it small. If you're just scalping or trading a bounce, think $100 for every $100,000 in an account, or one-tenth of 1%.

Don't take losses home. "If you buy something on Tuesday … if it's showing a loss by Friday, it has to trade."

Know your clock. Younger investors "can buy quality names and hold them forever." Near retirement, "your first order of business here is to play superior defense."

Story Continues

When in doubt, sit it out. "Harvest some cash here and wait."

Martin's last guideline comes from hedge fund legend Paul Tudor Jones: risk $1 only where you see $5 or more of upside, a risk-reward ratio of at least 5-to-1. It "doesn't mean it's gonna show up," Martin said, but the payoff has to be there before you trade.

"You need to see massive amounts of asymmetry in this type of a market."

news.Title: Why Marvell Technology Stock Fell Hard in October
news.Content:
Shares of Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL), a semiconductor company , plunged last month as investors fled AI stocks on fears that tech companies are overspending on infrastructure. Shares declined further at the very end of the month after Bloomberg reported that Marvell would buy optical component maker Lumentum .

Marvell stock finished the month down 25.6%, according to data provided by S&P Global Market Intelligence . Here's what investors need to know about Marvell's unimpressive share price performance.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Marvell fell on AI spending fears and acquisition news

Marvell stock started the month strong after the company's management announced at its investor day that fiscal 2027 revenue would increase by 45% to $12 billion and 2028 sales would rise another 50% to $20 billion.

What's more, Marvell's leadership said revenue in 2031 would be $80 billion at the midpoint of guidance, nearly 10 times the company's fiscal 2026 sales.

But Marvell shareholders quickly forgot all of that good news as AI stocks declined during the month. Investors have become increasingly skeptical that the hundreds of billions of dollars technology companies are spending on AI data center infrastructure will be worth it.

Bank of America estimates that AI companies could double their spending by 2028, reaching $2.1 trillion. That's a hefty price tag, and investor fears are colliding with the fact that inflation is on the rise, causing many to worry that interest rate hikes could slow the economy and make borrowing even more expensive.

Finally, at the end of October, Bloomberg reported that Marvell was in advanced talks to purchase component maker Lumentum . Marvell will pay for the acquisition in an all-stock deal and values Lumentum at $115 billion. Investors were unhappy with the news because the purchase could significantly dilute existing shareholder value.

Marvell stock remains volatile

Marvell stock started November with a rapid decline, as investors continued to process the news of the Lumentum acquisition and remained concerned about AI spending in general. But Marvell's shares began rising again today as some tech investors rushed back into artificial intelligence stocks, believing that the sell-off over the past month is overdone.

Story Continues

All of which means that Marvell stock could remain volatile over the short term as shareholders try to determine if its recent acquisition -- which is expected to be completed in the first half of 2028 -- is the right move and if the broader AI trade will remain shaky.

news.Content:
If we look at Cisco Systems (CSCO) strictly from a "data nerd" perspective, there may be a statistical likelihood that CSCO stock may move higher within the near-term time period. Of course, if we were simply placing a binary bet that the security will move higher from the current spot price, that might be an incredibly straightforward wager.

Unfortunately, the options market isn't in the business of providing easy wagers.

Let's lay down what we know. In the past 30 days, Cisco stock dropped nearly 21% due to macroeconomic concerns that have weighed heavily on artificial intelligence and related infrastructures. Naturally, the red ink imposed a penalty on CSCO's chart performance, causing the ticker to incur a 56% Sell rating from the Barchart Technical Opinion indicator.

On a conceptual note, the fallout presents a tempting proposition for contrarian options traders. As one of the giants in network infrastructure, Cisco's ever-growing relevance underpins capital inflows into CSCO stock. Therefore, mean reversion isn't just a random idea — it has real plausibility for a name like Cisco.

This observation leads to another fact: whenever the number of positive weekly candlesticks greatly outnumbers negative candlesticks over a rolling 10-week period, the historical tendency is for CSCO stock to rise higher than the random aggregate performance of any 10-week period (going back to the last five years).

Simply put, the observation of historical data suggests that there is typically a transition from an extremely bearish state to a future bullish state. In this particular circumstance — where Cisco stock has printed only three up weeks within a 10-week period — the probability of the ticker hitting the psychological target of $100 over the next five weeks is estimated at 46.7%.

From here, the narrative gets tricky.

CSCO Stock for the December Monthly Isn't a Good Deal

If we wanted to speculate on the above observation — that Cisco stock tends to transition from bearish to bullish states — the December monthly options chain (expiring Dec. 18) would presumably give us plenty of time. However, bull call spreads for that expiration period featuring a second-leg strike price of $100 only provide a maximum payout of 96.08% at time of writing.

Story Continues

From an expected value (EV) perspective, that's going to put our debit-based transaction into negative expectancy. I'm not saying that this idea is irrational as "rationality" is a philosophically relative term; what's rational to one person may be utterly bonkers to another. But if we both agree to use EV as a standard of rationality, then under that specific condition, the December monthly is not a good deal.

Shall we then extend the expiration date further out? That would lower time risk but would greatly escalate event risk — or the risk that plenty of stuff can happen between now and the January monthly chain. And because CSCO stock is such a stout investment overall, the market's expectation is for the security to recover by then. Subsequently, the payout for reaching $100 will be even lower, creating an even more negative expectancy.

It stinks but arguably, the more rational approach here is to consider the upcoming November monthly, which is only two weeks away. This reduces event risk (since there's less room for multiple variable events to materialize) at the expense of exponentially higher time risk.

However, the nuance here is the fiscal-first-quarter earnings disclosure scheduled for Nov. 12.

Is a Potential Upshot in the Works for Cisco Stock?

Right now, Barchart has the implied volatility (IV) for the November monthly chain at 73.41%. That's significant because the historical volatility reading for the period is only 38.92%. In other words, under baseline conditions, a standard bullish environment would likely have CSCO stock gradually drift higher. We're talking about a stock that features a 60-month beta of 1.01 — very much characteristic of a blue chip.

Obviously, anticipation is rising sharply ahead of the company's Q1 earnings report. Now, a high IV doesn't necessarily mean that CSCO stock will move northward; the volatility could just as easily send the ticker crashing down, particularly if results and/or guidance don't exceed the market's expectations.

Still, the contrarian viewpoint is as follows. Because Cisco stock has already incurred a heavy beatdown, it may only take a relatively small unit of good news to have a disproportionately positive impact on CSCO.

As for my personal speculation on the matter, I mentioned that Cisco's transitional dynamics lead to an estimated probability of 46.7% that CSCO stock will hit $100 over the next five weeks. It's possible, then, that this inferred move could occur over the next two weeks thanks to the potential earnings catalyst.

If you want to take a speculative shot, you may consider the 96/100 bull call spread expiring Nov. 20. With a maximum payout of 128.57% stemming from a $175 net debit, your EV would come out to $11.80 or a return on capital of +6.74%.

Granted, that's not the most attractive wager but it would keep you out of negative expectancy.

news.Title: Rambus (RMBS) Forms 'Hammer Chart Pattern': Time for Bottom Fishing?
news.Content:
Shares of Rambus (RMBS) have been struggling lately and have lost 12% over the past week. However, a hammer chart pattern was formed in its last trading session, which could mean that the stock found support with bulls being able to counteract the bears. So, it could witness a trend reversal down the road.

The formation of a hammer pattern is considered a technical indication of nearing a bottom with likely subsiding of selling pressure. But this is not the only factor that makes a bullish case for the stock. On the fundamental side, strong agreement among Wall Street analysts in raising earnings estimates for this memory chip designer enhances its prospects of a trend reversal.

Understanding Hammer Chart and the Technique to Trade It

This is one of the popular price patterns in candlestick charting. A minor difference between the opening and closing prices forms a small candle body, and a higher difference between the low of the day and the open or close forms a long lower wick (or vertical line). The length of the lower wick being at least twice the length of the real body, the candle resembles a 'hammer.'

In simple terms, during a downtrend, with bears having absolute control, a stock usually opens lower compared to the previous day's close, and again closes lower. On the day the hammer pattern is formed, maintaining the downtrend, the stock makes a new low. However, after eventually finding support at the low of the day, some amount of buying interest emerges, pushing the stock up to close the session near or slightly above its opening price.

When it occurs at the bottom of a downtrend, this pattern signals that the bears might have lost control over the price. And, the success of bulls in stopping the price from falling further indicates a potential trend reversal.

Hammer candles can occur on any timeframe -- such as one-minute, daily, weekly -- and are utilized by both short-term as well as long-term investors.

Like every technical indicator, the hammer chart pattern has its limitations. Particularly, as the strength of a hammer depends on its placement on the chart, it should always be used in conjunction with other bullish indicators.

Here's What Increases the Odds of a Turnaround for RMBS

An upward trend in earnings estimate revisions that RMBS has been witnessing lately can certainly be considered a bullish indicator on the fundamental side. That's because empirical research shows that trends in earnings estimate revisions are strongly correlated with near-term stock price movements.

Story Continues

The consensus EPS estimate for the current year has increased 4.8% over the last 30 days. This means that the Wall Street analysts covering RMBS are majorly in agreement about the company's potential to report better earnings than what they predicted earlier.

If this is not enough, you should note that RMBS currently has a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy), which means it is in the top 20% of more than 4,000 stocks that we rank based on trends in earnings estimate revisions and EPS surprises. And stocks carrying a Zacks Rank #1 or 2 usually outperform the market. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks Rank #1 (Strong Buy) stocks here >>>> .

Moreover, a Zacks Rank of 2 for Rambus is a more conclusive indication of a potential trend reversal, as the Zacks Rank has proven to be an excellent timing indicator that helps investors identify precisely when a company's prospects are beginning to improve.

news.Title: AAOI Stock Rises 7% Post Q3 Earnings: Should You Buy, Sell or Hold?
news.Content:
Applied Optoelectronics AAOI shares have risen 6.9% since it reported third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 5, 2026. The surge reflects robust demand for its data center and CATV products, driven by strong 400G and 800G transceiver shipments, AI infrastructure investments and increased sales of 1.8 GHz CATV amplifiers in the third quarter of 2026.

Click here to check the details of Applied Optoelectronics' third-quarter 2026 results.

Applied Optoelectronics stock has rallied 43.8% in the year-to-date period, outperforming the Zacks Computer & Technology sector's appreciation of 4.1% and the Zacks Electronics - Semiconductors industry's decline of 2.9%.

The outperformance can be attributed to robust demand for AAOI's high-speed optical transceivers, driven by accelerating AI data-center investments. Rapid adoption of 400G and 800G products, expanding hyperscaler relationships, and a multiyear agreement for 1.6T transceivers further strengthened its growth prospects. The company is also benefiting from increased manufacturing capacity and improving profitability.

AAOI Stock Performance

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AAOI Benefits From AI-Led Optical Networking Demand

Applied Optoelectronics is benefiting from accelerating optical networking demand, driven by artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure investments and hyperscale data center upgrades. The growing adoption of 400G, 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers is strengthening Applied Optoelectronics' position in the data center market and supporting robust revenue growth.

In the third quarter of 2026, data center revenues increased 254% year over year and 45% sequentially to $155.6 million. Revenues from 800G products nearly quadrupled sequentially to $47.5 million, while 400G revenues nearly doubled to $93.4 million. This momentum highlights strong demand for advanced optical connectivity solutions supporting AI workloads.

The company's growth prospects received a boost from a multi-year agreement with a Tier 1 hyperscale customer for 1.6T transceivers. AAOI expects this agreement to generate $1 billion to $1.5 billion in revenues through May 2029, subject to customer demand and supply conditions. The transition toward 1.6T products should support higher average selling prices and improved margins.

AAOI is aggressively expanding manufacturing capacity to capitalize on these opportunities. It expects monthly production capacity for 800G and 1.6T products to exceed one million units by the end of 2027. Growing opportunities in co-packaged optics and high-power lasers provide additional long-term growth avenues.

Story Continues

AAOI's Earnings Estimates Show Upward Trend

AAOI's robust demand for its next-generation data center products, particularly driven by the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and the company's continued product innovation, is expected to benefit the company's top-line growth.

For the fourth quarter of 2026, Applied Optoelectronics expects revenues between $385 million and $420 million. Datacenter revenues are projected to be between $270 million and $300 million, while CATV revenues are expected to be between $105 million and $115 million.

Applied Optoelectronics expects non-GAAP earnings per share in the range of 48 cents to 63 cents. The consensus mark for earnings is currently pegged at 59 cents per share, unchanged over the past 30 days. The company reported a loss of 1 cent in the year-ago quarter.

AAOI Faces Margin Pressure and Rising Competition

Despite its expanding portfolio, Applied Optoelectronics faced margin pressure in the third quarter of 2026 due to an unfavorable product mix. Non-GAAP gross margin declined to 28.7% from 31% a year ago, falling below management's guidance of 29-30.5%. A faster-than-expected customer transition from 800G to 1.6T transceivers resulted in lower-than-anticipated 800G sales and a higher proportion of 400G products. 100G transceiver revenues also declined as a customer faced switch shortages linked to industry-wide memory supply constraints. Manufacturing capacity limitations and supply-chain bottlenecks also restricted the company's ability to fully capitalize on strong demand.

AAOI is also suffering from stiff competition from companies like Fabrinet FN, Lumentum LITE, and Coherent COHR, which are also expanding their footprint in the optical networking market.

Fabrinet is benefiting from strong demand for AI-driven data center infrastructure, particularly data center interconnect, optical transceivers, and high-performance computing. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, Data center revenues jumped 78% year over year to $777 million. Data center revenues increased 16% sequentially and accounted for approximately 53% of total revenues.

Lumentum's expanding portfolio has been noteworthy. In October 2026, Lumentum announced a collaboration with Astera Labs and Corning to demonstrate 1060 nm VCSEL-based PCIe-over-optics connectivity at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The technology aims to improve bandwidth density, power efficiency, and signal quality while addressing connectivity challenges in large-scale AI infrastructure

Coherent is benefiting from strong AI infrastructure spending, rising demand for 800G and 1.6T optical transceivers, and growing adoption of optical connectivity across data centers. Rapid growth in its Scale Across business, the ramp-up of PhotonLink and optical circuit switches, and expanding indium phosphide manufacturing capacity are supporting revenue growth and margin expansion.

Applied Optoelectronics shares are also trading at a premium, as suggested by its Value Score of F.

What Should Investors Do With AAOI Stock?

Applied Optoelectronics' strong AI-driven optical networking demand, growing hyperscaler relationships and expanding manufacturing capacity support its long-term growth prospects.

Moreover, Wall Street's consensus price target implies roughly 211.19% upside from current levels.

However, margin pressure, supply-chain constraints and intense competition from companies like Fabrinet, Lumentum and Coherent remain headwinds.

Applied Optoelectronics currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold), suggesting that it may be wise to wait for a more favorable entry point in the stock. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: LRCX Gains 8% on a $25B Buyback Plan: Is the Stock Worth Holding Now?
news.Content:
Lam Research Corporation LRCX shares rose 8.2% last Friday, following the company's announcement of a massive $25 billion share repurchase authorization on Nov. 5. The move offered some relief to investors after a difficult period for the semiconductor equipment maker.

Since reporting its first-quarter fiscal 2027 results on Oct. 21, Lam Research shares had come under heavy selling pressure, losing 23.1% amid concerns over its near-term outlook. For the second quarter, Lam Research expects revenues of $8.6 billion, plus or minus $400 million, non-GAAP gross margin of 52.5%, non-GAAP operating margin of 40.5% and non-GAAP earnings per share (EPS) of $2.33, plus or minus 15 cents.

Although these projections indicate sequential growth and slightly higher margins, management acknowledged that supply-chain constraints would limit revenue potential. The outlook disappointed investors expecting stronger growth. The stock also came under pressure from a broader semiconductor sell-off, as macroeconomic uncertainties, profit-booking in AI infrastructure stocks and growing concerns over data center spending weighed on investor sentiment.

However, the latest capital return announcement has renewed some investor confidence. Lam Research's long-term business prospects remain encouraging, supported by rising AI-related chip demand and increasing semiconductor manufacturing complexity. Given its strong fundamentals and attractive long-term growth opportunities, investors should consider holding LRCX stock for now.

LRCX's Strong Q1 Performance Supports the Bullish Case

Lam Research delivered an impressive September quarter performance. Revenues increased 54% year over year to $8.22 billion compared with $5.32 billion in the year-ago quarter. Non-GAAP EPS surged 75% to $2.20 from $1.26.

Lam Research Corporation Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Lam Research Corporation price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Lam Research Corporation Quote

The company also reported a record non-GAAP gross margin of 52.4%, up from 50.6% in the prior-year quarter. Non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 40.2% from 35%. Operating margin crossed the 40% mark for the first time in the company's history.

Memory and foundry investments supported the strong performance. Memory accounted for 46% of systems revenues, with memory revenues increasing 120% year over year. NAND revenues rose approximately 40% sequentially, while foundry also delivered record revenues.

Lam Research's Customer Support Business Group ("CSBG") generated nearly $2.5 billion in revenues, increasing 40% year over year and marking its fourth consecutive quarterly record.

Story Continues

Robust AI Spending Supports LRCX's Long-Term Prospects

Lam Research's long-term growth prospects remain encouraging as AI adoption increases demand for advanced chips, memory and storage. Management expects worldwide wafer fabrication equipment (WFE) spending to reach the mid-$150 billion range in calendar year 2026, followed by more than $200 billion in 2027.

The company expects calendar year 2026 systems revenues to grow more than 40% year over year, marking its third consecutive year of outperforming the WFE market. Several technology trends support this outlook. Increasing demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM), advanced packaging, leading-edge foundry logic and next-generation NAND technologies is amplifying the need for sophisticated wafer fabrication equipment.

Lam Research is well-positioned to benefit from these developments through its deposition and etch technologies. Its Acara etch and Ether dry resist solutions are gaining traction in advanced chip manufacturing. Management now expects cumulative Ether-related revenues to reach approximately $2.5 billion by the end of this decade, around $1 billion above its previous expectation.

Lam Research expects its CSBG revenues to grow more than 15% year over year in calendar year 2027. This recurring service-related business provides an additional source of growth and helps reduce dependence on new equipment sales.

Management also believes the semiconductor industry is entering a multi-year investment cycle, with customer visibility extending through 2028.

LRCX's $25B Buyback Plan Strengthens Shareholder Returns

The latest capital return announcement provides another reason to remain invested in Lam Research. The $25 billion repurchase authorization supplements the remaining balance of approximately $3 billion from its previous authorization.

The company also declared a quarterly dividend of 33 cents per share, payable on Jan. 6, 2027. These initiatives reflect management's confidence in its cash generation and long-term business positioning.

Lam Research ended the September quarter with $7.45 billion in cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash compared with $5.60 billion in the June quarter. During the first quarter of fiscal 2027, the company's free cash flow reached a record $3.24 billion. It repurchased shares worth $1.01 billion and paid $325 million in dividends during the quarter.

LRCX's Valuation Looks More Attractive After the Decline

Valuation also supports holding Lam Research shares. LRCX trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings multiple of 19.26, higher than the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector average of 16.79. However, the current multiple is significantly below its one-year median of 35.39 and close to its one-year low of 17.82.

Lam Research Forward 12-Month P/E Ratio

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

This suggests that the recent correction has made the stock considerably more attractive from a valuation perspective. Given Lam Research's strong earnings growth, expanding margins and favorable industry outlook, its current valuation appears reasonable.

Compared with other semiconductor equipment makers, Lam Research trades at a lower multiple than ASML Holding ASML and KLA Corporation KLAC, while at a higher multiple than Applied Materials AMAT. At present, ASML Holding, KLA and Applied Materials trade at a forward 12-month P/E multiple of 23.64, 22.37 and 18.08, respectively.

Lam Research shares have outperformed the broader tech sector. LRCX stock has gained 17.1% year to date (YTD), significantly higher than the sector's 4.2% return. The stock has also surpassed the gains of KLA, but has underperformed ASML Holding and Applied Materials. Shares of ASML Holding, Applied Materials and KLA have soared 33.2%, 29.5% and 14%, respectively, YTD.

Lam Research YTD Price Return Performance

Conclusion: Hold Lam Research Stock for Now

Lam Research faces near-term challenges from supply-chain constraints and semiconductor market volatility. However, its record financial performance, strong AI-related growth opportunities, expanding service business and substantial shareholder return plans provide a solid long-term foundation. With its valuation also considerably lower than its 52-week average, investors should consider holding LRCX stock rather than selling into the recent weakness.

Lam Research currently carries a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold). You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here .

news.Title: Is Arm Stock a Buy on the Dip as Agentic AI Opportunity Emerges?
news.Content:
Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM) shares continued their rollercoaster ride this year, sinking after its Q3 earnings report came out on Nov. 4. The semiconductor stock still trades up more than 50% on the year, although it's down more than 60% from its 52-week high.

The latest dip came despite management saying it is now more confident it can secure enough supply to hit $2 billion in central processing unit (CPU) revenue across fiscal 2027 and 2028. With shipments set to begin later this calendar year, that is essentially five and a half fiscal quarters.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Arm has long used a licensing and subscription model, where it provides its IP (intellectual property) for customers to design their own chips. However, it surprised investors this year when it revealed that it would begin making its own chips for the first time, given the booming market in data center CPUs. At the time of the announcement, Arm projected that it would be able to take a 15% market share in what it saw becoming a $100 billion market by 2031. Since then, Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices have projected that the market will reach $220 billion by 2030, given the surge in agentic AI.

Arm claims that its Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) CPUs provide twice the per-rack performance of AMD's EPYC 9755 CPU. Notably, though, this is a chip introduced in late 2024, not one of its newer chips based on AMD's new Venice architecture, which is designed specifically for agentic AI. Arm has orders for its AGI CPUs from multiple customers through calendar 2027, with shipments expected to begin in Q4 2026.

However, demand for its AGI CPUs isn't the big concern with investors; it's whether the company can produce its chips in a tight market for components and fab capacity. As such, the company's comments that it was becoming more comfortable reaching its loftier $2 billion CPU goal should be viewed as a positive.

Meanwhile, ARM said that its data center royalty revenue doubled in the quarter. It believes this revenue will continue to grow in the triple digits over the next few years as data centers transition from x86 architecture, used by AMD and Intel CPUs, to ARM-based solutions. It said it has a 50% server market share among large hyperscalers at the end of 2025, rising to 60% by the end of 2026.

Story Continues

Arm's core business, meanwhile, remained solid in fiscal Q2. Overall revenue climbed 27% to $1.44 billion, while annualized contract value (ACV), which smooths out license revenue, rose 12%. License revenue surged by 50% year over year to $773 million. The company said this was $100 million more than expected due to customers signing long-term deals to access its technology. It signed three new Arm Total Access agreements in the quarter, bringing the total to 60, and four compute subsystem licenses. Large shareholder and partner SoftBank contributed $209 million in revenue in the quarter.

Royalty revenue, meanwhile, rose by 8% year over year to $670 million. The growth was driven by continued adoption of its higher-cost Armv9 architecture and Arm CSS platform and growing data center business. This helped offset weakness in the smartphone market.

Looking ahead, Arm forecasts fiscal Q3 revenue to come in around $1.54 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 24%. License revenue is projected to surge roughly 50%, while royalty revenue is expected to rise in the low single digits given the pressures in the smartphone and PC markets due to high memory prices. It guided for adjusted earnings per share to be between $0.52 and $0.60.

Is Arm stock a buy?

Arm is well positioned to be one of the biggest beneficiaries of agentic AI through a combination of its booming custom CPU business and starting to sell its own server CPUs. The company projects it can generate around $2 billion in incremental revenue from its new AGI CPU business over the next five quarters starting in its fiscal Q4. Meanwhile, if it can achieve a 15% market share, that would grow to more than $30 billion in revenue for a market projected to hit $220 billion in a few years. This should more than overcome any weaknesses in current smartphones and PCs.

The question really comes down to valuation and growth. Arm has always commanded a huge multiple given its IP royalty and subscription business model, but now that it's designing its own chips, its multiple should shrink. Currently, the stock has a forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of over 55 based on the fiscal 2028 (ending March 2028) consensus estimates. However, the longer-term consensus does not fully reflect the company's AGI CPU opportunity, with the fiscal 2031 analyst revenue estimate at just under $26 billion, though it could come in closer to $40 billion if things play out in its favor.

As such, I'd be a buyer of this AI stock on this recent dip, as it will likely look cheap in a few years if the AI build-out continues.

news.Title: Marvell Stock Fell 58% From Its Record. History Says What Followed Its Last 4 Drops This Deep.
news.Content:
Marvell Technology (NASDAQ:MRVL) stock had a terrible start to November. On Nov. 2, shares dropped around 13% as the chip designer agreed to buy optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock deal.

The slide went on after the Nov. 3 elections sparked worries that new state limits might slow the building of artificial intelligence (AI) data centers. On Nov. 5 alone, the stock lost 16%.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

At its $133.55 close that day, Marvell sat about 58% off its record close of $316.43 on June 4.

A drop this deep isn't new to Marvell. Since its stock began trading in June 2000, it's fallen 55% or more from a record close four other times, going by split-adjusted daily closing prices. Twice, it needed over five years to get back to a record. The other two times, it was back at one within around three years of its high.

What type of drop is this one?

Image source: The Motley Fool.

Two long waits

Marvell's first crash came during the dot-com bust. The stock sank around 92% from its Sept. 13, 2000, record close to its low on April 4, 2001.

And a 58% loss, which it hit in November 2000, was nowhere near the bottom. After that, shares dropped around 80% more.

The business wasn't the issue. Showing how fast Marvell was growing then, its revenue doubled to $288.8 million in the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2002, helped by its purchase of networking chip designer Galileo Technology. By fiscal 2006 (ended Jan. 28, 2006), revenue had hit around $1.7 billion. Even so, the stock didn't close at a new record until November 2005, over five years after its peak.

I'd say the 2000 share price had run so far ahead of the business that even growth like that needed years to catch up.

The second drop took much longer to make up. From a record close on Jan. 27, 2006, shares sank around 87% by Nov. 20, 2008, in the financial crisis. Once again, a 58% loss (hit in December 2007) came well before the bottom, with around 68% more to go.

This time, growth stalled. Marvell's revenue in fiscal 2009 (ended Jan. 31, 2009) came to around $2.95 billion. Twelve years later, fiscal 2021's total was around $2.97 billion. Not surprisingly, the stock went more than 14 years without a new record, finally beating its 2006 close in June 2020.

The last two crashes ended fast

Marvell's two latest drops played out very differently. Shares fell around 62% between Dec. 7, 2021, and Jan. 5, 2023, and around 61% between Jan. 23 and April 21, 2025. Each time, a 58% loss was close to the low -- shares fell only about 9% more in the first case and basically not at all in the second.

Story Continues

Revenue wasn't perfect in those years. Marvell's revenue climbed 33% in fiscal 2023 (ended Jan. 28, 2023), then slid around 7% the next year. But fiscal 2026 (ended Jan. 31, 2026), which included the April 2025 low, saw 42% growth to a record $8.2 billion, fueled by what management called robust AI demand.

And the stock followed. It closed at new records in November 2024 and April 2026, around two years and one year after each 58% mark.

Is Marvell stock a buy after this drop?

I think today's business looks far more like 2025 than 2008. Marvell's revenue growth is accelerating, from 28% year over year in fiscal 2027's first quarter to 37% in the second (ended Aug. 1).

On Nov. 2, the company said third-quarter revenue is tracking with its forecast of around $3.15 billion, which would mean growth of about 52%.

The price looks nothing like 2000's, either. At around $141, Marvell shares cost about 19 times the adjusted earnings expected from its own business in fiscal 2028 (the year ending in January 2028). At the June record, that same earnings estimate would put the price-to-earnings ratio near 43. In other words, investors today pay less than half as much as they did in June for the same expected profits.

Notably, the fall has mostly erased this year's rally, not years of gains. Marvell stock began 2026 around $85, so it's still up over 50% in 2026.

In the end, Marvell's history suggests the depth of a drop matters less than what revenue does next, and Marvell's revenue growth keeps speeding up. I think the stock is worth buying here.

Of course, a 58% loss was far from the bottom in two of the four past crashes, and the same might happen this time. That's why I'd space my purchases out over time.

news.Title: Arm and Qualcomm Lead Mobile Chip Design. 1 Stock Is the Better Buy.
news.Content:
The share prices of two mobile industry chip designers, Qualcomm (NASDAQ: QCOM) and Arm Holdings (NASDAQ: ARM), plummeted after they reported their quarterly earnings on Wednesday, Nov. 4.

Qualcomm stock was down roughly 14% after missing earnings estimates, while Arm stock also fell 14% on a weaker-than-hoped outlook. The lukewarm results happened to come out on a day when there was a massive post-election sell-off, with the Nasdaq Composite down roughly 1,000 points on Nov. 5, or about 4%.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

Is this a buying opportunity for either mobile chip provider ?

Arm stock has been a juggernaut

Qualcomm and Arm are market leaders in the industry, but they occupy different niches within the space. Qualcomm designs chips that are used in mobile phones and holds a market share of about 23%. It is second only to Taiwanese company MediaTek, which has a 31% share.

Arm designs the blueprints or architecture for mobile phone chips, which it licenses to companies like Qualcomm and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) that use the blueprints to design their chips. Arm has a massive 99% market share in mobile phone chip architecture. That moat is protected by the fact that Arm owns the intellectual property rights to the computer language and instructions that the chips use to run the mobile software. Competitors cannot build their own architecture to run apps without the language that Arm controls.

There has been a lot of legal back-and-forth between Qualcomm and Arm, with Arm suing Qualcomm in 2022 for trademark infringement over alleged use of its designs. Qualcomm then sued Arm in 2024 for violating its agreements by withholding support, among other charges. Last month, a jury voted in favor of Qualcomm with nominal damages awarded.

Since it went public in September 2023, Arm, based in the U.K., has been a juggernaut, fueled by its market dominance. It has posted an average annualized return of 47% over the past three years. Qualcomm has averaged a 9% return over the past three years.

The two stocks have been moving in different directions this year, with Arm stock up 55% year-to-date and Qualcomm stock down 8%. Will the latest earnings change the trajectory for one or the other?

Qualcomm stock is cheaper

Arm posted record revenue of $1.44 billion in its fiscal second quarter, which was up 27% year over year. Its licensing revenue jumped 50% to $773 million, while royalty revenue increased 8% to $670 million.

Story Continues

Adjusted net income was $566 million, or $0.52 per share, up from $0.39 in the same period a year ago. Both revenue and earnings beat analysts' consensus estimates.

For its Q3, Arm projects $1.54 billion in revenue and adjusted earnings of $0.56 per share. This beat consensus estimates of $1.53 billion in revenue and $0.55 per share in earnings. Shares were down on the slower, single-digit growth in royalty revenue and an outlook that perhaps didn't beat estimates by enough to satisfy its high P/E ratio of 220.

Qualcomm saw revenue decline 8% in the quarter to $10.44 billion, but that was higher than estimates of $10.12 billion. Adjusted earnings were down 28% year over year to $2.17 per share, which slightly beat estimates of $2.16 per share.

In its guidance for the current quarter, Qualcomm estimates revenue of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion, which is higher at the midpoint than estimates of $10.48 billion. However, earnings are targeted at $2.15 and $2.35, which would be below consensus estimates of $2.27 per share.

Are either of these stocks a buy?

Of the two, Arm is in a much better position to grow long-term due to its dominance in the moblie industry, but also its growth in other markets, namely in AI data center chip design. But it is just way too expensive right now to consider.

Qualcomm is much cheaper, trading at 19 times earnings, but it faces headwinds with rising supply costs and that's putting a squeeze on earnings.

I wouldn't buy either right now, but you may want to revisit Arm stock after this sell-off to see if it settles at a more reasonable valuation.
